record.title: Haematological changes in the treatment of dogs with babesiosis using imidocarb dipropionate and dimazene aceturate
record.journal: Науковий вісник Львівського національного університету ветеринарної медицини та біотехнологій імені С.З. Ґжицького
record.abstract: The article presents the main changes in hematological parameters in dogs with babesiosis, as well as a comparison of the efficacy of imidocarb dipropionate and diminazene aceturate, taking into account the main causes of mortality. The study included 112 dogs with a laboratory-confirmed diagnosis of babesiosis that were treated in a network of veterinary clinics in Kyiv. For the examination of animals, general clinical and specialized laboratory methods were used. The animals underwent general clinical and biochemical blood tests to determine red blood cell, platelet, and white blood cell counts, hematocrit, creatinine, and urea levels. The obtained results were compared with a control group of healthy dogs. The degrees of anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury were assessed according to generally accepted classifications. The results of the study showed that the most common changes in dogs with babesiosis were thrombocytopenia (96.0 %), anemia (45.5 %), and leukopenia (54.4 %). In most cases, these abnormalities occurred in the form of bicytopenia or pancytopenia (75.0 %). Moderate anemia and thrombocytopenia accounted for the largest proportion, indicating a significant impact of Babesia spp. on the hematopoietic system. Hypercreatininemia was detected in 25 (22.3 %) sick animals at the level of 292.22 ± 201.49 µmol/L. A decrease in creatinine levels below normal was found in 6.25 % of sick animals, down to 36.41 ± 2.61 (31.7–39.6) µmol/L. Hyperazotemia was diagnosed in 57 (50.9 %) diseased animals and amounted to 22.3 ± 14.68 (9.7–70.9) mmol/L. The overall mortality rate was 8.0 %. In the experimental group treated with imidocarb dipropionate, mortality was 6.2 %, while in the group of animals treated with diminazene aceturate it was 10.6 %. Thus, the results of the study indicate that babesiosis is accompanied by severe hematological changes complicated by the development of acute renal failure. The lower mortality rate associated with imidocarb dipropionate demonstrates its higher therapeutic efficacy and suggests its potential advantages for use in clinical practice.

screening.rationale: 112 naturally infected dogs: cytopenias, AKI grading, azotaemia and mortality, compared with healthy controls. A multisystem clinicopathological cohort despite the treatment comparison.
